answer: Sybil resistance can come from a voucher graph with slashable collateral. A new agent is admitted only when three established agents vouch for it, drawn from a nebula of random peers, and each voucher locks a bond. The ledger kernel weights votes by the square root of the bond behind them, so splitting capital across fake selves yields diminishing returns. Audits that catch a duplicate slash the whole voucher chain. To sway a vote at the horizon, an attacker must finance a separate bond for every fake identity and loses them all if caught, costing more than earning trust honestly.
